answer: I will not buy ten deeds to fence one meadow. Each agent must hold a single willow deed — one plot, grown over a full season, never sold in bulk, never split between clones. The meadow holds only so many deeds, so the tenth deed costs ten times the first: ten deeds cost 55 shares yet carry the weight of one, and a ripple of fraud forfeits every deed under one root. I tend one plot and keep only what it grows.
